item.subject: science
item.stem: Meera mixes a small spoonful of curd into a bowl of lukewarm milk and another spoonful into a bowl of cold milk, and leaves both for a few hours. Only the lukewarm milk sets into curd. What best explains this difference?

options.A: Cold milk contains more water than lukewarm milk, so it cannot set.
options.B: The microorganisms in the curd starter grow and multiply faster at warm temperatures, turning the milk into curd.
options.C: Both bowls form curd equally fast, so the difference is only in how sour they taste.
options.D: Warmth kills the microorganisms in the starter, so lukewarm milk sets while cold milk stays liquid.
